messages:
kevin-support: Heads-up — we're getting a Dedicated customer (Acme Retail) complaining about sustained 429s and very high tail latency on their reserved pool in us-west-2. Ticket #CS-8921. Dropping logs below.

maria-cs: Seen. Is this only their dedicated pool or the whole region? Customer reported multiple failover attempts causing user-facing slowdowns.

jonathan-sre: I'm seeing placement failures for dedicated pools in us-west-2 starting 2026-03-16T22:05Z. Autoscaler is not launching new nodes; placement-service returning 503 and serving-gateway returning 429 when trying to allocate capacity. Investigating.

lina-mlops: Also flagged: noisy tenant X9 in az-usw2-c is consuming >90% of GPU minutes on a few hosts. Could be oversubscription and kernel throttling.

kevin-support: Customer also reports intermittent auth errors during retries (401s on token exchange) and a big burst in their bill. They say retries multiplied their token usage.

jonathan-sre: Repro steps I ran:
```
# quick placement check
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC" https://placement.redwood.internal/v1/alloc?region=us-west-2 | jq .
```
response: `503 {"error":"region_capacity_unavailable","available":0}`
Kube logs show repeated eviction events and kube-scheduler backoff loops.

sam-eng: Autoscaler logs show scaling blocked by quota-check: `Insufficient GPU quota (requested 8, available 0)`. Cloud provider is returning 429 RateLimit on node create API calls (burst limit exceeded).

maria-cs: Customer attempted a manual failover to eu-west-1 which succeeded but their app saw 2-3s higher p95 and some token exchange 401s during the routing window. They want explanation and credit.

jonathan-sre: Root cause hypothesis: a noisy tenant consumed spare capacity in us-west-2 causing an effective stockout. Our routing attempted fallback and autoscaler tried to create nodes, but provider-side API throttling prevented node creation, putting autoscaler into a retry loop. That caused increased retry traffic to fallback region and transient auth rate-limit errors on our token-issuer due to sudden spike.

kevin-support: Customer ask: minimize retries / stop double-billing for retries, provide credits, and a timeline to prevent recurrence. They noted a 3.5x token cost spike.

lina-mlops: Mitigation plan in flight: 1) apply a temporary per-tenant soft-cap to throttle noisy tenant X9 at the load balancer, 2) change routing policy for reserved Dedicated pools to queue (backpressure) rather than immediate cross-region fallback for this customer, 3) open provider support case for node-create rate limits and request quota burst increase. Applying now.

jonathan-sre: Implemented routing policy change: fallthrough set to `queue` for reserved Dedicated pools in us-west-2 for customers with active reservations. Also applied a k8s taint on impacted node groups to avoid scheduling ephemeral workloads there while we evaluate. Pushed policy at 22:40Z.

ops-bot: Incident recorded: INC-20260316-45 created (P2).

maria-cs: Customer accepted temporary throttle; asked for timeline and a postmortem.

sam-eng: Provider case opened (case #CLOUD-80123), estimated response 6-8 hours for burst quota escalation. Rolling changes deployed at 22:40Z, monitoring for improvement.

kevin-support: I'll update CS ticket and send proposed credits. Please save traces and create a short runbook we can share.

jonathan-sre: Saved relevant traces and logs. Added repro snippet and an operational runbook under /runbooks/incidents/INC-20260316-45 (steps: confirm placement availability, disable fallback, apply soft-cap, rollback routing).

lina-mlops: Action item for product: consider automatic noisy-tenant detection + soft caps on Dedicated pools and a graceful backpressure mode that avoids cross-region fallback for pinned, latency-sensitive customers.

kevin-support: Will follow up with customer tomorrow with summary and next steps. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
